Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FIXED PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT FOR SCHOOLS 

PART II CLIMBING ROPES 



Til 



n 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



1. Scope — Requirements for climbing ropes used in conjunction witii steel tubular playground 
equipment erected in school premises for school children up to the age of 12 years. 

2. Terminology — For the purpose of this standard, the following definition in addition to those 
given in IS : 3871-1966 * Glossary of terms relating to fibre ropes and cordages ' shall apply. 

2.1 Climbing Rope — A rope, the upper end of which is made attachable to a horizontal steel tube 
by the riveting of a clamp through the rope and the lower end of which is treated to prevent the 
strands from unravelling. 

3. Material 

3.0 General— In addition to the relevant requirements given in 2 of IS : 8404 ( Part I )-1977 * Speci- 
fication for fixed playground equipment for schools; Part I General requirements \ the requirements 
given in 3.1 to 3.1.5 shall apply, 

3.1 ffope — Hemp or flax as ordered by the purchaser. Rope fibre shall be clean and free from 
dust, dry pulp or any other foreign matter. 

3.1.1 Whipping -— Tarred hemp or flax twine. 

3.1.2 Clamp — Mild steel or wrought iron. 

3.1.3 Rivets — Mild steel. 

3.1.4 Leather — Chrome-tanned cow/buff hide or synthetic leather. 



2 A. 5 Cotton ^/?reac/— Conforming to Variety No, 35 [! 
' Specification for cotton sewing threads {first revision)\ 



tex X 8 (6^/8)] of IS ; 1720-1969 



4. Construction 

4.1 Climbing ropes shall be four-strand, shroud-laid, with or without heart as ordered. 

4.2 Top end of the climbing rope shall be bound with tarred twine which shall extend to a distance 
of 228 mm along the surface of the rope. A clamp shall be fitted over the rope and secured by 
three rivets, 6 mm in diameter. 

4.3 Lower end of the climbing rope shall be finished by one of the following methods: 

a) A leather cap, double sewn on to the rope. Before applying the cap lower end of the 
rope shall be bound either with tarred hemp or flax twine, 

b) A sail-maker's whipping. 

c) Either a back splice or a tapered back splice having at least two full tucks followed by at 
least two further tucks for each of which one-third of the strands of the free ends are cut 
away, 

d) Tapered ends, if specially ordered. 

4.4 Stopper knots shall not be used. 



Adopted 20 December 1979

IS : 8404 (Part II) -1979 

5. Dimensions 

5.1 Rope — Diameter of the rope shall be 35 mm to 40 mm. Length of the rope shall be as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier. However, unless specifically ordered by the purchaser, 
the length shall be such that when fixed to the supporting steel tube, lower end of the rope shall be 
not less than 300 mm and not more than 450 mm above ground level. 

5.2 Leather Cap — Thickness of leather— 1'5 to 2*0 mm, overall length = 100 ± 2 mm minimum, 

6. Marking — The climbing rope shall be suitably attached with a tag marked with manufacturer's 
name, initials or registered trade-mark. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking— Details available with the Indian Standards Institution, 

7. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
